title: VISTA: Optimizing GPU Scheduling through Versatile Locality-Aware Data Sharing
problem: GPU thread scheduling typically overlooks data locality patterns across non-adjacent warps and CTAs, missing opportunities to reduce memory traffic through intelligent scheduling that exploits non-adjacent data sharing.
motivation: GPU memory efficiency is critical for performance and energy in high-memory-bandwidth workloads; unexploited data locality between non-adjacent threads represents a significant optimization opportunity.
method: VISTA is a GPU scheduler that watches for data-sharing patterns between warps (groups of 32 threads) and CTAs (larger thread blocks) during execution, even when those warps or blocks aren't next to each other in the GPU's execution order. Once it spots these patterns, VISTA reschedules the work so that computations that access the same data run closer together in time. This keeps the data they need in the GPU's fast cache memory longer, cutting down on expensive memory traffic that would otherwise slow down memory-intensive programs.
key_novelty: VISTA detects at runtime when non-adjacent warps and CTAs share data, then schedules them together to reduce memory accesses.
contributions: VISTA smart locality-aware GPU scheduler detecting data sharing patterns across non-adjacent warps/CTAs
Dynamic runtime information used to guide scheduling decisions for improved memory efficiency
48.1% performance improvement in memory-intensive GPGPU applications
51.8% energy reduction with negligible hardware overhead
limitations: Not discussed; evaluation on memory-intensive GPGPU workloads without broader application coverage.
primary_theme: Locality-aware GPU scheduling exploiting non-adjacent data sharing
